sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of M.V.Act, 1989 claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- in respect of accidental injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. In the petition it is stated that on 08.02.2022 at 1.00 am (midnight) petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider in Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-13-ET-9898 along with his friend Sumanth C.P on 27th cross, jayanagar 6th block, Bangalore.

Sumanth was riding motor cycle at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner without observing traffic norms and when he reached near Avathi Nilaya, at that time all of a sudden a dog came from opposite direction in front to their bike Sumanth tried to avoid hitting the dog and applied brake and he lost control over his vehicle and came on wrong lane and hit against the road divider due to which, petitioner fell down from the motor cycle and sustained grievous injuries to his head and right leg.
Immediately he was shifted to Digvijaya hospital, Bangalore for first aid and then he was shifted to Supra hospital for better treatment.
He was admitted as an inpatient and took treatment.
Still he is bed ridden and under treatment.
He spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment (SCCH-12) 3 MVC.No.1406/2022 and in future he has to incur for future medical expenses also and he suffered permanent disability.
He is unable to lead a normal life as earlier and not able to do his work.
He suffered huge loss of income due to accident.
3. He was working as Food delivery boy and earning income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he is not able to work and not able to do other activities.
That the cause of accident is due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of Motor Cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 13-ET-9898.
The Jayanagara traffic police have registered case in Crime No. 30/2022.

1st respondent is the insurance company and 2nd respondent is the owner of motor cycle therefore,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, both respondents are served and Respondent no.1 and 2 appeared before this court through their respective counsel and have filed written statement separately.
5. Respondent no.1 insurance company in its written statement contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further it has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-ET-9898 and liability to indemnify the 2nd respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, provisions of M.V.Act, valid and effective driving license held by the rider of motor cycle, R.C and F.C and also subject to (SCCH-12) 4 MVC.No.1406/2022 confirmation of Section 64 VB of Insurance Act.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act.
Further 2nd respondent has not complied provisions of Sec.134(c) and police have not complied 158(c) of IMV Act.
Right reserved to contest the matter U/Sec.170 of M.V.Act.

That the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving license and thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
That in order to get unlawful gain petitioner has created false story of alleged accident by implicating the rider of motor cycle.
That petitioner himself was riding the vehicle and solely negligent in causing the accident, the rider of motor cycle is not covered under the policy.

On all Harshith.R vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190441344/
2 these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

sentences.text: 6. Respondent no.2 in its written statement contended that petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
That the statement made in the petition are denied.

He contended that, rider of motor cycle is an experienced rider who was having driving license to ride the said motor cycle and he was moving slowly towards the deceased house by following all traffic rules in a moderate speed, it is very unfortunate the dog all of a sudden came to the middle of the road and all preventive measure was taken by applying brake and finally lost the control and the rider after 13 days died at Apollo hospital, Bannerghatta road, Bangalore and this petitioner sustained simple injuries and the rider of the vehicle is not responsible (SCCH-12) 5 MVC.No.1406/2022 and the said vehicle insured with 1 st respondent insurance company and the said policy was covered for the said vehicle as on the date of accident as such 1st respondent is liable to pay the compensation and the petition is to be dismissed against 2 nd respondent.
Age, occupation and income of the petitioner is denied.
Treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses alleged by him are disputed.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessors- in-office has framed following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that the injuries shown in petition are sustained by him when he was proceeding in a motor cycle as a pillion rider in which accident occurred on 08.02.2022 due to rash and negligent riding of his friend who was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-13-ET-9898 in order to avoid a dog which came in front of their bike the rider applied sudden brake and lost control over the vehicle and hit against a road divider and caused accident, due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner prove his age, occupation, income and permanent disability if any?
3. Whether the 1st respondent proves that the driver of motor cycle bearing No.KA-13-ET-9898 did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident ?
4. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?

5. What Order or Award?
Harshith.

9. Heard learned counsel for both sides and perused records.

On taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence placed before this Tribunal and on hearing arguments, my answers to the above issues as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: In the Negative  Issue No.4: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.5: As per final order, for the  following;
 REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of petitioner that he is pillion rider in motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-ET-9898 and on 08.02.2022 at 01.00 am himself and rider of motor cycle was riding on 27th Cross, Jayanagar 6th Block, Bangalore and at that time one dog came in front of his vehicle and rider of the vehicle could not control the vehicle and applied brake and he lost control and hit against a road divider and sustained grievous (SCCH-12) 7 MVC.No.1406/2022 injuries.
To prove these facts, petitioner entered witness box and got examined as P.W.1.
In his chief examination he reiterated petition averments.

To prove negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle, he produced FIR, first information, sketch,
spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, final report and discharge summary of Supra hospital are produced at Ex.P.1 to 8.
They show that, petitioner himself has given first information to police and his statement is recorded before the doctor in the hospital.
In the first information he stated that he was pillion rider on motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-ET-9898 and one Sumanth C.P was riding it.

When they reached near Jayanagar 6 th block, rider of the motor cycle was riding the same in high speed, in rash and negligent manner and at that time, one street dog came in opposite direction of the motor cycle and the rider tried to avoid hitting the dog, suddenly applied brake and he lost control over his bike and hit to a road divider.
Due to this accident petitioner sustained severe injuries and rider fell unconscious on the spot.
Further he was shifted to Digvijay hospital and took treatment then he was shifted to Supra hospital for higher medical treatment.
It is further stated in the first information that accident is due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle Sumanth C.P. and action may be taken against him.
On the basis of said information Jayanagar Traffic police have registered case in Crime No.30/2022 against the rider of motor cycle Sumanth C.P.
The spot sketch is prepared and it shows accident is not due to any mechanical defect in the vehicle.
As per spot mahazar it is tar road having divider and footpath on (SCCH-12) 8

sentences.text: There is tyre marks on the road.
There is also street light poles nearby.
12. Wound certificate produced by the petitioner shows alleged history of RTA on 08.02.2022 at 01.00 am and petitioner was brought to hospital on the same day in the morning 7.00am.
That injury no.2 i.e., fracture of right femur is grievous in nature and as per final report rider of vehicle was found to be negligent and charge sheet is filed case against him.
Further it is stated that the rider expired on 21.02.2022 as he could not survive from the treatment and petitioner herein who is pillion rider sustained injury to his right leg.
It is also mentioned in the final report hat both the rider and pillion rider were not wearing helmet.
In the discharge summary produced by the petitioner it is mentioned as RTA on 08.02.2022.

On the basis of these documents it can be seen that, on that day which petitioner and rider of two wheeler was traveling on the road, considering the late night 01. am there is no possibility of having heavy traffic and the rider of motor cycle could have maintained control over the vehicle had he maintained low speed.
Instead, he lost control over the vehicle and hit a divider to avoid hitting street dog.
It appears that he was in high speed and therefore he could not control the vehicle.
That is nothing but pure negligence on the part of the two wheeler rider.
That final report also shows both petitioner and rider were not wearing helmet which has caused them severe injuries.
Therefore, in the opinion of this court negligence on the part of the two wheeler is established by the petitioner.
In the cross examination nothing could be elicited to deny the accident or to (SCCH-12) 9 MVC.No.1406/2022 dispute the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Therefore, the negligence on the part of the rider of two wheeler is established by the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer this issue in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2 :
Respondent no.2 disputed the age of the petitioner in the written statement.
To prove his age, petitioner has produced his aadhaar card at Ex.P.10.
It shows that he was born on 15.08.1997 Accident took place on 08.02.2022.
He was aged 24 years at the time of accident.
Therefore, the age of the petitioner is considered as 24 years at the time of accident.
14. In respect of occupation it is stated that, petitioner was working as Food Delivery Boy and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To prove this fact he has not produced any document.
Further in his cross examination he stated that at the time of accident he was II yr law student at R.V. Law College.
In his first information also he stated that he is law college student and not mentioned about his occupation as food delivery boy.
Further he stated in the cross examination that he dropped the college but not produced any documents to that effect.
The suggestion that he is still student is denied.
He denied that he is not delivery boy at Zomato as alleged in the petition.

In the present case there is no document to show petitioner is either student or delivery body, but he is aged 24 years by that time he would have completed his degree and there are all chances that he was working as delivery boy.

Hence, when there is no document to show either he is student or delivery boy considering his age and circumstances of the (SCCH-12) 10 MVC.No.1406/2022 case this court comes to the conclusion that his occupation is delivery boy.
As there is no document to show his income, notional income of Rs.16,000/- is adopted.
15. In respect of permanent disability a doctor by name S.A.Somashekar is examined as P.W.2.

He is Orthopaedic Surgeon at Bowring Hospital, Bengaluru Doctor has assessed the disability of Harshith.R vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190441344/

sentences.text: In his chief examination he stated that petitioner has sustained fracture of right distal femur and he underwent surgery.

On his recent examination petitioner complaints that he has pain in right leg, limping, gross wasting of right thigh and swelling of right leg, shortening,
deformity of right leg seen, surgical scars are present over right thigh and knee.
P.W.2 has assessed total disability of right lower limb at 45% and 23% to whole body.
Petitioner is said to be a Delivery boy and said disabilities come in the way of his working.
It is settled law that, doctor can only assess physical disability and cannot assess the functional disability having regard to avocation of the patient.
In the cross examination of P.W.2, such assessment made by the doctor is disputed by the both respondents.
In view of the fracture in right lower limb petitioner suffers permanent disability and it may affect any occupation as delivery boy.
Hence, In the opinion of this court functional disability affecting the income of the petitioner 10% having regard to young age of the petitioner and there are chances of fast recovery.
Accordingly, I answer this issue Partly in the Affirmative.
(SCCH-12) 11 MVC.No.1406/2022 16. ISSUE NO.3 : 1st respondent disputed the driving licence of rider of motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-ET-9898.
But to prove this fact no evidence is led by 1st respondent, hence he has not proved this issue.
Accordingly, this issue is answered in the Negative.
17. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of above reasons, injuries sustained by petitioner are due to the accident caused by the rider of motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-ET-9898.
There is nexus between the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the accident.
Hence he is entitled to compensation at the hands of respondents.

The quantum of compensation is determined as under:
(i) For Medical expenses: The petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.13.
Totally he has paid amount of Rs.1,86,603/- as per Ex.P.13 medical bills.
The said payment of bill is due to the accident caused to him.
They are subsequent to the date of accident.
Though they are disputed, no satisfactory material is placed to disbelieve the bills.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.1,86,603/-.
(ii) For Food and nourishment:
The petitioner was admitted to Supra hospital from 08.02.2022 to 13.02.2022.
He was in hospital for 06 days.
Accident took place in the year 2022.
Since he was in hospital, food and nourishment charges will have to be awarded.
Considering the cost of living, and food, nourishment charges if per day Rs.300/- is awarded it will meet (SCCH-12) 12 MVC.No.1406/2022 the ends of justice.
Hence for food and nourishment Rs.300/- x 06 days = Rs. 1,800/-is awarded.
(iii) For Attendant charges:
For a period of inpatient for 06 days someone should have looked after petitioner in the hospital.
Even if his family member has taken care of him in the said period, that family member's income for those days is lost.
Hence per day if Rs.300/- is awarded as attendant charges in 2022, it will meet the ends of justice.
Hence for attendant charges Rs.300/- x 06 days =Rs.1,800/-is awarded.

sentences.text: (iv) For Loss of income during laid up period:
As per the finding to issue No.2, the income of the petitioner per month is. Rs.16,000/-.
He was inpatient for 06 days and he was advised to take rest also he underwent operation.
Minimum 2 months is required to recover from such operation in view of grievous injury.

Therefore, laid up period of petitioner is considered as total 3 months including in patient period and loss of income during laid up period is Rs.16,000/-x 3= 48,000/- He is entitled to Rs.48,000/- as loss of income during laid up period.
(v) Conveyance charges:
It is stated that petitioner was shifted to Supra hosptal.
He has spent money for conveyance for the purpose of treatment.
Considering all those conveyances, in the opinion of this tribunal if an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded it will meet the ends of justice.
(vi) Loss of future income due to Disability :
As per the findings given to issue no.2 functional disability of the petitioner is assessed at the rate of 10%.

Therefore, loss of future income (SCCH-12)
13 MVC.No.1406/2022 due to disability is to be calculated as income per month Rs.16,000 X 12 months X 10% disability X appropriate multiplier to the age group of 15-25 is 18.
Hence, in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.3,45,600/- towards loss of future income due to disability.
(vii) For Future medical expenses:
P.W.2 has stated that petitioner needs to remove the implants which may require Rs.40,000/- but no estimation is produced.
In view of necessity of removal of implants for well being of the petitioner in the opinion of this court amount of Rs.25,000/- shall be awarded for future medical treatment.
Accordingly, Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
(viii) For Pain and sufferings:
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The records show that he underwent operation and implants are in situ.
He was in Supra hospital from 08.02.2022 to 13.02.2022.
As per discharge summary produced at Ex.P.8 petitioner underwent surgery to right lower limb and continued follow up treatment.
Therefore, for pain and suffering the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- .
(ix) Physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life :

As per the evidence of assessed doctor,
petitioner complained about pain and difficulty.
He underwent operation and suffers discomfort.
Meaning, he cannot lead the normal life as he used to live before the accident.
Certainly accident has caused physical discomfort and came in the way of normal enjoyment of (SCCH-12) 14 MVC.No.1406/2022 life of petitioner.
Hence in the opinion of this court, petitioner is entitled to compensation under the head of physical discomfort and loss of amenities of life.

Under the said head he is entitled for Rs.50,000/-
(x) Loss of future prospect:

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme court, even in injury cases,
loss of future prospect has to be considered.
But in the present case, the on going through the evidence of assessed doctor and the nature of injuries sutained by the petitioner there is no chance of loss of future prospect.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:-

Therefore, I hold that the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.6,93,803/- in respect of injuries sustained by him in the Road traffic accident.
18. Liability: Since Respondent no.1 has admitted the insurance policy, he is liable to indemnify the insured.

Hence, I answer this issue "Partly in the Affirmative".
19. ISSUE NO.5:-

In view of above reasons I proceed to pass following :
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,93,803 /- with interest @ 6% pa on the amount of Rs.6,68,803/- from the date of petition till the date of payment.
(Future medical expenses of Rs.25,000/- will not carry interest).from the hands of respondents.
The respondent no.1 insurance company is liable to indemnify the insured and directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Out of compensation amount with cost and interest awarded to the petitioner 50% is ordered to be released in his favour and Harshith.
